description: The platforms the kinematic brain firmware can be built for, as numbers a program can read: the device, the clocks, the kernel clock and the bit timing of the stack bus, the owner of each host-facing peripheral and the role of the host link. tools/platform_profile.py reads it and tests/test_platform_profiles.py computes what each profile gives (the bit rate of the stack bus, the sample point, the clocks that must agree) and compares it with docs/bus_contract.json. Evidence: simulator (host tests of the numbers); nothing here has run on a board and the values taken from the CubeMX project are candidates until a bench row confirms them.

h745_current.status: what the firmware in this repository is built for today

not_memory_mapped.name: NOR_FLASH_SPI5
not_memory_mapped.source: HYDRA_UMC_H757_NETS.txt, step 10: the GD25Q128E NOR flash is on SPI5 in standard SPI mode (not memory mapped)
not_memory_mapped.note: an external storage on SPI5 (6.25 Mbit/s in the CubeMX project), read and written through the SPI5 driver; the earlier note that called it QSPI is wrong

contradictions_with_the_h745_repository: the H745 repository has no external memory at all; the H757 board has 256 MiB of SDR SDRAM on FMC (two banks of 128 MiB) that no linker script or driver uses yet
the migration note called the NOR flash QSPI; the board documents put it on SPI5 in standard SPI mode, so it is not memory mapped and needs no linker region
the CubeMX project gives every pin to the CM7 (the owner decided the CM7 owns SPI1, FDCAN1 and I2C4); the H745 repository gave them to the CM4 and let the CM7 reach them through the mailbox

controller_board.note: the controller board has two FDCAN controllers: FDCAN1 on STACK A towards the brain and FDCAN2 on the downlink towards its tool head; both run at 1 Mbit/s (the tool head bus moved to 1 Mbit/s by decision of the owner, the 500 kbit/s of the earlier URTC protocol is a legacy value of the CAN contract and is not used here)
